archetype.name: Rebuilding Year (bottoming out)
archetype.definition: Brooklyn's third straight losing season and its worst yet: a 20-62 year where one productive wing and a couple of efficient bigs couldn't offset the league's least effective offense and a guard group that graded last.

report.headline: Third straight slide: a bottom-ranked offense and a guard corps that couldn't hold up

recap.finish: 20-62; fifth in the Atlantic, missed the postseason
recap.body:
This was a team that couldn't score. Brooklyn finished 30th of 30 in ORtg at 108.7, against a league average of 115.8, and last in both eFG % (52) and TS % (55.9). The shot diet was built around the arc: a 3PA Rate of 45.5 ranked sixth in the league. The shooting to justify it never came, with a 3P % of 34 that ranked 29th. Add a TOV % of 14.3, 29th in the league, and too few possessions ended in good shots. The slow pace (97.1) made the scoreboard look less dire than the ratings. Points allowed a game ranked 17th, but the 119 DRtg ranked 26th, and opponents shot 38.1% from three, the worst mark in the league.

The season opened 0-5 and was 3-16 by the end of November. Then came the one stretch that looked like a different team. December went 7-4, with only 104.64 points allowed a game, the stingiest month by a distance. It didn't hold. January went 3-14, February 2-10 and March 3-14, and the team was 15-44 by the end of February. The longest winning streak all year was three games, the longest losing streak ten. December reads as an outlier, not a turning point.

The roster split cleanly by group. The wings graded B+, carried by Michael Porter Jr., who scored 1,259 points at a 59.5 TS % on a 30.5 USG %. That made him 13th of 96 on the small forwards tab, with a BPM of 3 and the team better by 5.9 with him on the floor. The frontcourt graded D-, but that hides its best piece. Day'Ron Sharpe posted a 63.8 TS %, a BPM of 1.4 and a team-best On-Off of 6.8. Nic Claxton led the roster with 4.8 Win Shares. The grade was dragged down by the power forwards, with Clowney, Wolf and Wilson all ranked in the bottom half of their tab.

The backcourt was the real failure, an F grade with only 1 Win Share combined across its four listed players. Nolan Traoré ran a 22.8 USG % on a 47.9 TS % with a BPM of -6.8. Drake Powell's On-Off was -8.1. Egor Dëmin was the exception, the best-ranked guard on the roster with 124 threes and an On-Off of 4.7. The defense leaked to the same spots: shooting guards scored 2.3 points above their own averages against Brooklyn, 28th in the league by that measure, and small forwards' raw scoring against them ranked 30th.

The ending was as flat as the middle. The Nets went 3-7 in their last ten, losing by 13.7 a game, 3.71 points worse than their season margin. The finale was a 136-101 loss in Toronto. Even 20 wins slightly flattered them: W vs Pt Diff was +2, and the margin implied 18.

highlights.title: Porter Jr. carried the wings
highlights.body: The B+ wing grade was largely one player. Porter Jr. scored efficiently on heavy usage, ranked 13th of 96 small forwards, and the team was better with him on the floor. It was the one group that looked like an NBA-average unit or better.

highlights.title: Sharpe and Claxton anchored the middle
highlights.body: The listed frontcourt produced most of the roster's Win Shares. Claxton led the team and Sharpe was its most efficient scorer with the best On-Off. The D- grade comes from the power forwards, not the centers, so the two bigs are a real base to build from.

highlights.title: A December that held teams down
highlights.body: The 7-4 December came with the season's best defensive month by points allowed. It proved the floor wasn't always this low. But it was surrounded by losing months on either side, so treat it as variance rather than a template.

lowlights.title: Worst offense in the league
lowlights.body: Brooklyn ranked last in ORtg, eFG % and TS % while taking one of the league's highest shares of threes and missing most of them. This continues a trend rather than starting one: the offense ranked 28th a year earlier on a nearly identical 3PA Rate. Without better shooting or shot creation, the volume-three approach just produces empty possessions.

lowlights.title: A guard group that graded F
lowlights.body: The four listed guards combined for 1 Win Share. Traoré was used heavily at a very low TS % with the worst BPM on the roster. Powell's minutes came with a deeply negative On-Off. Dëmin was the only guard whose numbers pointed upward.

lowlights.title: Perimeter defense got shot through
lowlights.body: Opponents posted the league's best 3P % against Brooklyn. Shooting guards scored well above their norms, and the DRtg slipped from 115.8 the year before to 119. The slow pace hid it in per-game points, but per possession this defense was bottom-five.

arc.note: An 0-5 start and 3-16 November gave way to a 7-4 December. The team then lost steadily through the final four months and finished 3-7 with its worst margins of the year.

recap.nextYear: The numbers leave a short list of keepers and a long list of needs. Porter Jr. was the offense, Sharpe and Claxton were the only efficient frontcourt minutes, and Dëmin was the lone guard with positive impact. The backcourt (F) and the power-forward spots behind the D- frontcourt grade are where the minutes have to get better. Nothing in the record was bad luck: W vs Pt Diff was +2, the margin implied 18 wins, and Net Rtg fell from -7.3 to -10.3. The history shows a fourth straight year of decline from the 45-37 team of 2022-23. The shooting and ball security, last- and near-last in the league, are the core problem to fix, not a slump to wait out.

confidence.note: Full 82-game season with consistent signals across ratings, grades and months.
